model: Smart-UPS with Network Management Card 2 / 3 (BACnet IP)
applies_to: APC Smart-UPS units (SMT, SMX, SRT, SURT, SURTD and others) fitted with a Network Management Card 2 (firmware 6.5.6 or later) or Network Management Card 3.
summary: The APC Network Management Card in a Smart-UPS serves BACnet IP. The object list is fixed by the card firmware: Analog Values for runtime, battery, input, output and load readings plus outlet-group and shutdown settings; Binary Values for outlet states, test commands, option enables and about 170 UPS alarm flags; Character String Values for identity text; and Multi-state Values for UPS state, UPS control and outlet-group control. Each object is only present on the UPS families marked in the table.
firmware: NMC2 application firmware 6.5.6 or later (sumx); NMC3 below 3.0 (su). See notes for NMC3 3.1.
notes: Instances are the NMC2 / NMC3 (< v3.0) index column. NMC3 firmware 3.1 renumbers some objects: BV 51-68 move up by 1 and BV 69-237 (alarm flags) move up by 2; MV 13-14 move up by 1; CSV 27-34 move up by 2. Index 47 'UIO probe 1 contact 1 severity' prints as 48 in the v3.1 column.
NMC3 v3.1 also adds objects that have no index on older cards: spot fluid sensor enables, alarms (BV 240-241 in v3.1), name/location text values and status MVs. They are not listed here.

Bracketed text in a description names the UPS families that support the object; objects marked for an AP9631/AP9635 card need the Universal I/O probe port. Alarm flags (BV 69-237) carry no model column in the document.
Multi-state option lists are given in the printed order; the document does not print state numbers.
Alarm flag BVs send event notifications to the recipients in the Default Notification Class (NC 0).
Some names are printed with typos (e.g. 'AbnormaOutputVoltage', 'ParalletlCommCondition2', 'Outlet group switched 3load shed runtime remaining'); they are kept as printed.

source.title: BACnet Application Map for Network Management Card 2 and 3 (Smart-UPS)

integration.summary: Enable BACnet on the Network Management Card (sumx/su firmware) and give the card a unique device instance. Read UPS state (MV 5), runtime remaining (AV 0), battery charge (AV 66), load (AV 19) and the alarm flags such as OnBattery, LowBattery and Overload. UPS Control (MV 6) and the outlet-group control MVs switch the UPS or its outlets, so restrict who can write them.

minimum_points.name: UPS state
minimum_points.why: Online, on battery, bypass, fault and so on

minimum_points.name: Output watts phase 1
minimum_points.why: Load as % of the watt rating

minimum_points.name: LostUPSComm
minimum_points.why: Card lost communication with the UPS

integration.enable: BACnet IP is part of the NMC2 'sumx' and NMC3 'su' application firmware and is turned on in the card's configuration. No BMS enable point is needed; UPS Control (MV 6) acts directly on the UPS.
setup: BACnet IP only; BACnet is configured on the Network Management Card (device instance and related settings are covered in the NMC User Guide).
Check the UPS model prefix on the UPS label (SMT/SMX/SRT, SURT, SURTD) to know which objects it will have.
On NMC3 firmware 3.1, read the object list again: several BV, MV and CSV instances shift (see notes).
Alarm BVs can send event notifications; add the BMS as a recipient of NC 0 DefaultNotifier.
gotchas: Writing UPS Control or an outlet-group control MV can switch off the protected load.
BV 23-26 start real UPS tests (self test, alarm tests, runtime calibration); BV 27 cancels a running test.
Universal I/O probe objects exist only with an AP9631/AP9635 card and a probe fitted.
Instances differ between NMC2/NMC3 below 3.0 and NMC3 3.1 for alarm flags; remap after a card firmware upgrade.
